candidates.snippet: Invalidating the cached entry at write time keeps readers from ever observing a stale value, which is what makes the backing store authoritative in practice.
candidates.title: Invalidate on write, not on read

candidates.snippet: Feed the starter twice a day at room temperature; it is ready when it doubles within four hours.
candidates.title: Sourdough starter schedule

focus.content: A write-through cache forwards every write to the backing store before acknowledging it, so the store is always the source of truth and a cache loss costs nothing but latency.
focus.title: Write-through cache keeps the store authoritative

candidates.snippet: WAL removes reader/writer blocking but writers still take the single write lock, so two processes inserting at once queue behind each other.
candidates.title: WAL still serialises writers

candidates.snippet: Postgres gives each transaction a snapshot of row versions so readers never block writers; old versions are vacuumed later.
candidates.title: Postgres MVCC snapshots

focus.content: With journal_mode=WAL, readers see a consistent snapshot while a writer appends to the log, so a reporting query no longer blocks on an in-flight insert.
focus.title: SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers

candidates.snippet: The enrich worker retries a failed item after 0.5 s, then 1 s plus a random 0-250 ms, then gives up after three attempts.
candidates.title: Enrich worker retry schedule

candidates.snippet: A fixed five-second retry interval is simpler and, in our load tests, retry collisions never mattered, so jitter is unnecessary complexity.
candidates.title: Fixed-interval retries are sufficient

focus.content: When many clients fail at once, retrying on the same schedule makes them collide again; adding random jitter to the backoff spreads the retries out.
focus.title: Retries with jitter avoid thundering herds

candidates.snippet: Typed-edge inference will not run a call unless the day's ledger is under the configured ceiling; exhaustion skips synthesis observably.
candidates.title: Edge inference checks the budget first

candidates.snippet: Remove suckers below the first flower truss so the plant puts its energy into fruit rather than foliage.
candidates.title: Pruning tomato plants

focus.content: Admission is checked before each call and the actual spend recorded after it, so the ledger can overshoot the ceiling by at most one call's tokens.
focus.title: The daily token budget is a soft ceiling

candidates.snippet: Each edge the adjudicator writes carries provenance_type inferred, so retrieval can filter it out and a human-asserted edge wins any conflict.
candidates.title: Edges written by the adjudicator are marked inferred

focus.content: Every edge the adjudicator writes is marked inferred so retrieval can filter it and a human assertion always wins on conflict.
focus.title: Inferred edges are written with provenance_type inferred

candidates.snippet: Degrease the chain, dry it fully, and apply one drop of lubricant per roller before wiping off the excess.
candidates.title: Bicycle chain maintenance

candidates.snippet: Prick the warm cake all over and pour the lemon syrup slowly so it soaks in rather than running off.
candidates.title: Lemon drizzle cake

focus.content: Three outcomes for the quarter: ship the eval suite, migrate the adjudicator to a cheaper model, and label the first golden set.
focus.title: Quarterly planning note
